explication:
<explanation>
1. Project type and purpose  
   - DiscordChatExporter is a cross-platform client application (desktop GUI and CLI) that exports message history from Discord channels.  
   - It’s organized as three main deliverables:  
     • DiscordChatExporter.Gui – the Avalonia-based desktop UI  
     • DiscordChatExporter.Cli – the command-line interface  
     • DiscordChatExporter.Core – the shared library containing domain models, Discord API client, exporters, filters, and format writers  

2. High-level layers & components  
   - Presentation Layer  
     • CLI (Program.cs + Commands/*)  
     • GUI (App.axaml, ViewModels/*, Views/*, Services/*)  
   - Application Layer  
     • Command handlers (ExportCommandBase, DiscordCommandBase)  
     • DialogManager, ViewManager, SettingsService, UpdateService  
   - Domain/Core Layer  
     • DiscordClient (HTTP wrapper over Discord REST API)  
     • Data models under Discord/Data (Message, Channel, Guild, User, Embeds, etc.)  
     • Exporting pipeline (ExportContext → MessageExporter → format‐specific writers: CsvMessageWriter, HtmlMessageWriter, JsonMessageWriter, PlainTextMessageWriter)  
     • Filtering (MessageFilter AST, grammar parser)  
     • Partitioning (FileSizePartitionLimit, MessageCountPartitionLimit)  
     • Markdown parsing/rendering (MarkdownParser, MarkdownVisitor, HtmlMarkdownVisitor)  
   - Infrastructure Layer  
     • HTTP utilities (in Core/Utils/Http.cs)  
     • File system & path utilities (PathEx, UrlBuilder)  
     • Docker support (dockerfile, docker-entrypoint.sh)  
     • CI/CD (GitHub workflows, Dependabot)  

3. External dependencies & services  
   - Discord’s REST API (HTTPS endpoints) – the data source  
   - Local file system – export destination  
   - Docker hub – optional containerized CLI  
   - GitHub Actions – build/test/release pipeline  

4. Diagramming guidance  
   a. Main components to represent  
      – User (actor)  
      – CLI UI & GUI UI  
      – Command/Controller modules  
      – Core library (DiscordClient, Export pipeline, Filters, Writers)  
      – Discord REST API (external service)  
      – File system (local storage)  
      – CI/CD pipeline (optional – GitHub Actions, Docker)  

   b. Relationships & data flows  
      1. User → CLI or GUI (input triggers)  
      2. CLI/GUI → Command Handler → Core API  
      3. Core → DiscordClient → Discord REST API (HTTP request/response)  
      4. Core → ExportContext → MessageExporter → Writers  
      5. Writers → File system (writes export files)  
      6. GUI may invoke UpdateService to check GitHub Releases  

   c. Architectural patterns & principles  
      – Layered architecture (Presentation → Application → Domain → Infrastructure)  
      – Command pattern for CLI commands  
      – Dependency inversion: Core library does not depend on UI  
      – Single Responsibility: separate classes for data models, exporting, filtering, rendering  

   d. Key technologies & frameworks  
      – C#/.NET 6+  
      – Avalonia UI (GUI)  
      – Spectre.Console.CommandLine or similar for CLI binding  
      – Razor templates (.cshtml) for HTML Preamble/Postamble  
      – Superpower-based parser for filters & markdown  
      – GitHub Actions for CI/CD, Docker for containerization  

5. Tailoring the diagram  
   - For this full-stack (UI + core library) client application:  
     • Use two parallel UI blocks: “CLI” and “GUI”  
     • Show both calling into the same “Core” block  
     • Emphasize the Core’s interactions with Discord API and file system  
   - Omit low-level class lists; instead group by feature areas (Data, Exporting, Filtering, Markdown)  

6. Visual elements to include  
   – Clear rectangular boxes for components (UI, Core modules)  
   – Cylinders for storage (File system) and external service icons for Discord API  
   – Directional arrows: label with method calls or data flow (e.g., “FetchMessages()”, “WriteHtml()”)  
   – Color coding:  
     • Blue for UI components  
     • Green for Core/domain modules  
     • Gray for infrastructure (HTTP, FS)  
     • Orange for external services (Discord API, GitHub Actions)  
   – Legend explaining colors/shapes  

7. Level of detail  
   - Capture each major submodule (DiscordClient, Exporting.Pipeline, Writers, Filtering, Markdown)  
   - Do not overload with every single class; focus on logical groupings  
   - Show both CLI and GUI feeding into the same Core library to underline code reuse  

By following this structure, your system design diagram will clearly expose the layered architecture, data flows from user to Discord and back to disk, and highlight the separation of concerns between UI, application logic, domain services, and infrastructure.  
</explanation>
